newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa trades lower on disappointing Q3.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa trades lower on disappointing Q3.

text.p: Shares of Aluminum Co of America were down 3-1/4 at 57-1/8 at midday Friday after the company reported lower than expected third quarter results.

"This is the kind of market that has no interest in companies without earnings momentum," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "The pressure is for short-term performance."
Alcoa reported third quarter earnings per operating share of $0.77, compared to the First Call estimate of $0.95 before a special after-tax charge of $65.5 million, or $0.38 a share.
"There is a lot of selling," one trader said. "It remains to be seen whether the stock will just continue to get slammed down or whether some people will take advatage of the price."
Alcoa said the strike at its Cleveland forging plant cut third quarter earnings by $6.5 million, or $0.04 per share.
Metz said the company's longer-term prospects were still good and that Alcoa was well-positioned in terms of demand and pricing power and had low inventories.
"But no one is interested in the long-term right now on Wall Street. If you want to keep your job you have to perform well this week," he said.
